title: Godot 4 (GDScript) → Unreal Engine 5 (C++ / Blueprint)
conventions: A GDScript on a scene root usually becomes an Actor class (AMyThing : public AActor, or ACharacter/APawn for controllable bodies); reusable behaviour on child nodes becomes UActorComponent/USceneComponent classes. Each class is a .h + .cpp pair inside Source/<Module>/.

Godot scenes (.tscn) become Blueprint classes deriving from the C++ class, or levels (.umap). ReversePort writes a scene spec (JSON) with converted transforms; build the Blueprint in the editor from it.
Coordinates: Unreal is left-handed, Z-up, X-forward, centimeters. From Godot: (x, y, z) m → (-z, x, y) × 100 cm. Use port_convert for positions and rotations.
Godot's Camera3D fov is vertical; Unreal's FieldOfView is horizontal: hfov = 2·atan(tan(vfov/2)·aspect). port_convert {fov} does this.
Every exposed property needs UPROPERTY(...), every bound/blueprint-callable function UFUNCTION(...), and the class GENERATED_BODY(); include "<Name>.generated.h" last in the header.
Unreal ticks are frame-rate based by default; move fixed-step logic into Tick with DeltaTime or enable physics substepping.

entries.to: UCLASS() class AX : public AActor { GENERATED_BODY() … };
entries.notes: CharacterBody3D → ACharacter; RigidBody3D → AActor with a simulating UStaticMeshComponent root; Area3D → AActor with UBoxComponent/USphereComponent (overlap).
